summary: Use a valid regular expression.
Use valid template syntax.
Use a valid time parsing layout.
Encode fixed-width values with encoding/binary.
Specify the unit when writing a sleep duration.
Pass the executable and its arguments separately.
Print variable text without treating it as a format string.
Use a valid URL.
Use canonical HTTP header capitalization for direct map access.
Pass a positive match limit or -1 for every match.
Pass valid UTF-8 to string operations that inspect characters.
Pass a non-nil context to context-aware operations.
Pass the seek offset before the origin constant.
Pass a pointer to the decoding destination.
Stop tickers explicitly in modules targeting Go 1.22 or earlier.
bad:
// In a package targeting Go 1.22 or earlier.
func wait() { <-time.Tick(time.Second) }

summary: Subscribe to a signal that the process can receive.
Buffer channels passed to signal.Notify.
Request replacements instead of passing a zero replacement limit.
Use the supported replacement for a deprecated API.
Use a valid host and port in network addresses.
Compare IP addresses with net.IP.Equal.
Copy an io.Writer input before modifying its bytes.
List each character once in a trimming cutset.
Avoid relying on Timer.Reset's return value in code targeting older Go versions.
Marshal supported data types instead of channels or functions.
Align 64-bit atomic values on 32-bit architectures.
good:
type State struct { count atomic.Int64; flag bool }
state.count.Add(1)

summary: Pass a slice to sort.Slice.
bad: sort.Slice(42, func(i, j int) bool { return i < j })
good: sort.Slice(values, func(i, j int) bool { return values[i] < values[j] })

summary: Use a distinct key type for context values.
good:
type accountKey struct{}
context.WithValue(ctx, accountKey{}, account)

summary: Pass a supported base and bit size to strconv functions.
Encode into a destination that does not overlap the input.
Pass the actual error before the target error to errors.Is.
Increment a wait group before starting the goroutine.
Perform the protected operation between locking and unlocking.
Fail a test from the goroutine that runs the test.
Defer Unlock after calling Lock.
Propagate TestMain's exit status in test packages targeting Go versions before 1.15.
bad:
// In a test package targeting Go versions before 1.15.
func TestMain(m *testing.M) { m.Run() }

summary: Let the test framework control the benchmark iteration count.
Compare the intended operands instead of repeating one expression.
Copy the pointed-to value instead of taking its original address.
Compare unsigned values against values in their supported range.
bad:
var count uint
if count < 0 { return }
good:
var count uint
if count == 0 { return }

summary: Allow a loop to process more than its first element.
Use a pointer receiver when a method updates its receiver.
bad: func (state State) SetCount(count int) { state.count = count }

summary: Use or check a returned value before overwriting it.
bad:
value, err := read()
value, err = readAgain()
return value, err

summary: Update the variable that controls the loop.
bad: for i := 0; i < len(values); index++ { use(values[i]) }
good: for i := 0; i < len(values); i++ { use(values[i]) }

summary: Use the supplied argument before replacing it.
bad: func double(value int) int { value = 2; return value * 2 }
good: func double(value int) int { return value * 2 }

summary: Return or use the slice created by append.
Use a labeled break when exiting an outer loop from a switch.
Test for NaN with math.IsNaN.
Use the Boolean value directly instead of negating it twice.
Use distinct conditions in an if and else-if chain.
bad: if value == 1 { first() } else if value == 1 { second() }
good: if value == 1 { first() } else if value == 2 { second() }

summary: Avoid rounding an integer after converting it to a float.
Use bitwise operands that change the result.
Use the result returned by a function without side effects.
Assign a different value instead of assigning a variable to itself.
Include each build constraint once.
Test specific types before interfaces that already include them.
Assign the original slice when append adds zero elements.
Check a pointer value instead of comparing a variable's address to nil.
good: func missing(value *State) bool { return value == nil }

summary: Check the concrete pointer before converting it to an interface.
good:
var pointer *State
if pointer == nil { return }

summary: Compare builtin results against values they can return.
Use floating-point division when the result requires a fraction.
Construct negative zero with math.Copysign.
Encode the updated query and assign it to URL.RawQuery.
Use a meaningful divisor when computing a remainder.
Call a sorting operation instead of converting the slice type.
Pass an upper bound greater than one when requesting random alternatives.
Use newly allocated values without checking them against nil.
Use a supported runtime operating system or architecture identifier.
Allocate a map before assigning its entries.
Check the open error before deferring Close.
Block while waiting instead of running an empty loop.
Run cleanup within an endless loop instead of deferring it until the function returns.
Wait on a channel instead of repeatedly selecting an empty default branch.
Use the finalizer argument without capturing the object under finalization.
Provide a terminating condition for recursive calls.
Use valid Go struct tag syntax.
Match formatting verbs to their argument types.
Assert only interfaces with compatible method signatures.
Pass an even number of strings when an API expects pairs.
Compile the regular expression before checking values in a loop.
good:
pattern := regexp.MustCompile("^[a-z]+$")
for _, value := range values { use(pattern.MatchString(value)) }

summary: Convert bytes to a string directly in the map lookup.
Store a pointer in sync.Pool to avoid an additional allocation.
Range over the string directly when reading its runes.
Compare strings without case distinctions with strings.EqualFold.
Write bytes with io.Writer.Write.
Complete deferred cleanup during each iteration of a channel range.
bad: for value := range values { defer release(value) }

summary: Write file permissions as octal values.
Handle the condition instead of leaving an empty branch.
Apply the intended type to every constant in the group.
Export struct fields that must appear in marshaled output.
Convert to a wider integer before calculating high bits.
Delete a task-specific temporary directory instead of the system temporary directory.
Use the original interface value in the failed type assertion branch.
bad: if value, ok := input.(int); ok { use(value) } else { use(value) }
good: if value, ok := input.(int); ok { use(value) } else { use(input) }

summary: Write compiler directives without a space after the comment marker.
Defer the returned cleanup function's call.
Import packages without dot aliases.
Write error messages without initial capitalization or trailing punctuation.
Use a receiver identifier that identifies the receiver type.
Return the error as the final result.
Use a duration variable identifier without a misleading unit suffix.
Begin error variable identifiers with err or Err.
Use HTTP status constants.
Place the default switch case first or last.
bad: switch value { case 1: first(); default: other(); case 2: second() }
good: switch value { case 1: first(); case 2: second(); default: other() }

summary: Write the variable before the constant in comparisons.
Escape invisible characters in string literals.
Import each package once.
Omit a variable type that the initializer already determines.
Use plain channel send or receive instead of single-case select.
Replace for loop with call to copy.
Omit comparison with boolean constant.
Replace call to strings.Index with strings.Contains.
Replace call to bytes.Compare with bytes.Equal.
Drop unnecessary use of the blank identifier.
Use 'for { ... }' for infinite loops.
Simplify regular expression by using raw string literal.
Return the Boolean expression directly.
good: func ready(value int) bool { return value > 0 }

summary: Omit redundant nil check on slices, maps, and channels.
Omit default slice index.
Use a single append to concatenate two slices.
good:
x = append(x, y...)
x = append(x, y...)
x = append(x, y...)

summary: Replace time.Now().Sub(x) with time.Since(x).
Use a type conversion instead of manually copying struct fields.
Replace manual trimming with strings.TrimPrefix.
Use 'copy' for sliding elements.
Simplify 'make' call by omitting redundant arguments.
Omit redundant nil check in type assertion.
bad: if _, ok := i.(T); ok && i != nil {}

summary: Merge variable declaration and assignment.
Omit redundant control flow.
Replace x.Sub(time.Now()) with time.Until(x).
Don't use fmt.Sprintf("%s", x) unnecessarily.
Simplify error construction with fmt.Errorf.
Range over the string directly.
Use bytes.Buffer.String or bytes.Buffer.Bytes.
Omit redundant nil check around loop.
bad: if values != nil { for _, value := range values { use(value) } }

summary: Use sort.Ints(x), sort.Float64s(x), and sort.Strings(x).
Delete a map entry without checking whether it exists.
bad: if _, exists := entries[key]; exists { delete(entries, key) }

summary: Use result of type assertion to simplify cases.
good: if text, ok := value.(string); ok { use(text) }

summary: Let HTTP header methods canonicalize their key argument.
Use a map's zero value instead of guarding its lookup.
bad: if _, exists := counts[key]; exists { counts[key]++ } else { counts[key] = 1 }

summary: Sleep with time.Sleep instead of a single-case timer select.
Print the formatted text directly.
Use an existing string without calling fmt.Sprint.
Use an interface value without asserting it to its existing type.

summary: Apply De Morgan's law to negate the individual Boolean operands.

summary: Convert if/else-if chain to tagged switch.
bad: if value == 1 { first() } else if value == 2 { second() }
good: switch value { case 1: first(); case 2: second() }

Expand call to math.Pow.

Merge conditional assignment into variable declaration.
